summary: This work establishes a quantitative theoretical framework for understanding capacitive loading in superconducting circuits, deriving analytical relations between finite qubit capacitance budgets and achievable qubit-coupler coupling strengths. The framework identifies pad-to-ground participation as geometrically optimizable and inter-pad participation as limited by Josephson-junction parasitic capacitance, enabling design principles that achieve two-qubit MAP gates as fast as 27 ns with leakage infidelity below $10^{-3}$ in highly connected 2D fluxonium architectures.
motivation: Scaling fluxonium quantum processors to highly connected 2D lattices requires strong qubit-coupler interactions, but the intrinsically limited capacitance budget of fluxonium qubits ($C_q^\mathrm{eff} \sim 14$–$24$ fF) constrains achievable coupling strengths, making capacitive loading a critical bottleneck for fast two-qubit gate operations.
method: The authors develop circuit-QED analysis of symmetric dumbbell-floating, grounded, and concentric-floating fluxonium geometries, deriving compact expressions for effective capacitances and coupling strengths. They decompose loading into participation ratios: $C_{ab}/C_q^\mathrm{eff}$ (inter-pad, dominated by junction parasitic capacitance $C_{ab}^{J,\Sigma} \sim 4$ fF for $E_J/h = 5$ GHz) and $C_{bg}/C_{bg}^\mathrm{eff}$ (pad-to-ground, suppressible via geometric optimization to $< 0.1$). Electromagnetic simulations validate analytical predictions and optimize layouts achieving $J_{qc}/h \approx 900$ MHz versus 470 MHz in conventional designs.
result: For a representative optimized $5q4c$ unit cell with double-transmon couplers and improved junction process ($0.6 E_J/(h \cdot \mathrm{GHz})$ fF parasitic capacitance), statistically sampled two-qubit gates over 180 nearest-neighbor pairs achieve $t_\mathrm{gate}^* = 27$ ns at the 95th percentile with leakage infidelity $< 10^{-3}$ under 5% fabrication variations; extension to six-neighbor hexagonal architectures maintains $J_{qc}/h \geq 535$ MHz across all couplings.
